newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wills takes action against Philip Morris.
newsitem.headline: Wills takes action against Philip Morris.

text.p: Cigarette manufacturer W.D. & H.O. Wills said on Monday it had launched proceedings against Philip Morris Ltd for misleading and deceptive conduct and 'passing off' Wills' value brand Horizon.
Wills said it discovered last week that Philip Morris planned to launch a cigarette brand packaged almost idientically to Horizon in terms of colour, lettering and imagery.
Wills said Horizon had been the fastest growing cigarette brand in the Australian market and had achieved a 14 percent maket share since its launch in 1991.
"We will use every available means to protect Horizon from attack by this me-too product," Wills corporate communicaitons manager Catherine Byrne said in a statement.
Wills, 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc, reported a A$13.27 million profit in calendar 1996, up from a loss of A$5.16 million in 1995, which was due to a price war.

Philip Morris's Australian subsidiary chief, Henry Goldberg, said in April tha he expected another cigarette price war to erupt in Australia by June that could cost the sector A$100 million in earnings in 1997.
Rothmans Australia Ltd is the other main cigarette manufacturer in Australia.
